text:
Mohit: Bringing up smokestack-11b (checkpoint v2) — noticed subtle phase-shift in attention after q4-int8 quantization. Looks like prefix tokens start to wander after ~1k tokens. Anyone who can run runtime compat checks?
Carla: @Mohit can you paste the minimal repro? sample prompt + config?
Mohit: repro:
```
model: smokestack-11b-v2
quant: q4_0
seq_len: 2048
prompt: "User: Tell me a long story..."
```
Outputs drift after 1100 tokens.
Alyssa: Is this consistent between CPU fallback and GPU runtime?
Mohit: GPU only so far. CPU fallback produces less visible drift but is much slower.
Dmitri: Could be a position-encoding mismatch: model trained with ALiBi-ish slope? Any metadata on pos-enc from the hub?
Mohit: Hub metadata says learned absolute pos-emb with rotary-style embeddings applied to queries only. No explicit ALiBi.
Alyssa: @runtime-ci can you run a quick trace of KV indexes and attention phase at step 1000-1200? Look for key cache shifts or off-by-one in rotary application.
runtime-ci: started trace job 8402. Will post diff of kv indices and attn norms.
eval-bot: baseline evals (fp16): ppl=9.2 @ 1k tokens; q4_0: ppl=11.0; q4_0 + prefix caching tweak: ppl=10.1
Carla: interesting — eval shift suggests quantization interacts with pos-enc. What about preprocessing tokenization differences?
Mohit: tokenizer identical. I double-checked. Same merges and vocab.
Dmitri: Hypothesis: during KV reorder we may be dropping high-precision phase for certain heads when using pack-quant kernels. Suggest a patch: force fp32 rotary multiplies on critical heads and rerun.
Alyssa: can you try patch locally? If it reduces drift, we should add a temporary compatibility flag in runtime to force fp32 for rotary ops until we mitigate in kernels.
Mohit: testing now. If good, I'll open an intake ticket and mark priority P1 for bring-up — affects long-context agents.
Carla: add a small smoke test to eng-ml/ci: generate 1300-token continuation and assert no token-level perplexity regression > 5% vs fp16 baseline.
Dmitri: also capture attention-head-wise cosine similarity across token positions. Attach to the ticket.
runtime-ci: trace complete. Observed KV indices match expected ordering, but one kernel path (q4-multihead) clamps rot-phase to int16 during accumulation.
runtime-ci: attaching snippet:
```
head 3: rot_phase_fp32_mean=0.0023
head 3: rot_phase_q4_accum_mean=0.0011
```
Alyssa: that looks like numerical underflow from accumulation. Try Dmitri's fp32 rotary patch.
Mohit: patch applied locally, quick run: ppl=9.5 @1k tokens, drift reduced significantly.
Mohit: I'll open ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RW-2345 and add test links & runtime PR ref.
Carla: thanks — please @mention eng-runtime and eng-ml in the ticket. Also flag for on-call kernel owner.
Mohit: done. tagging @eng-runtime. Assigning to Dmitri to follow-up on kernel PR.
Dmitri: I'll prepare kernel PR with opt-in flag and perf microbench. If we can get <3% perf regression on hot path, propose merging.
Alyssa: good plan. If we can also add an automated quant-smoke in model onboarding checklist, that would prevent regressions.
Mohit: agreed. I'll update onboarding checklist with a 'long-context quant smoke' step.
Carla: nice work team :tada:
